Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning was used to optimise the number of trainable parameters and to perform less computationally expensive training. Our proposed model -TransProtFam could come up with accuracy scores of 99.43%,90.85% and 84.49% at family, sub-family and sub-subfamily levels, which exceeds the state-of-the-art neural network models. Our findings and the finetuning process we employed may provide insights into utilising large models trained on protein sequence corpora for specific tasks in Bioinformatics and related domains.

Author Keywords: Protein family classification and Deep Learning

articleTitle: Unified Detection Framework for Robbery Events: Integrating YOLOv8, Fast R-CNN, and RetinaNet with Explainable AI Validation and Real-time Android Application Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This research proposes a Unified Detection Framework for Robbery Events by combining YOLOv8, Fast R-CNN, and RetinaNet models. The framework incorporates Explainable AI Validation for transparency and real-time detection capabilities. Additionally, an Android application integration is implemented for practical deployment. Through experimentation and evaluation, the effectiveness of the framework in detecting robbery events is demonstrated. The fusion of multiple object detection models enhances accuracy and efficiency, while the integration of explainable AI validation ensures interpretability of results. The proposed framework shows promising results for addressing security concerns in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Fire and Smoke Detection using an Enhanced YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Due in part to global warming, the frequency of wildfires has increased in recent years, significantly impacting humans, wildlife, and forest ecosystems. To address this challenge, using technology for early fire detection through smoke can help firefighters and other stakeholders limit their spread and reduce the impact. In this research, we adopt the latest object detection model - YOLOv8 and use a fine-tuned version for detecting smoke and fire using the latest datasets. YOLOv8 backbone begins with two convolutional (Conv) layers, followed by a series of alternating Conv layers and C2F modules, and ends with a Spatial Pyramid Pooling - Fast (SPPF) module. Our improvement involves adding two extra Conv layers at the beginning of the backbone, between the alternating sequence of Conv and C2F layers. As the smoke and fire detection problem involves searching for smaller objects in the image, increasing the feature extraction layers improves the performance of smoke and fire detection. The fine-tuned model is tested with the FASDD v4 dataset, which depicts fire, smoke, non-fire, and non-smoke scenarios.

Author Keywords: Fire and Smoke Detection and YOLOv8

articleTitle: Enhancing Early Detection of Pancreatic Cancer: A Machine Learning Approach with Explainable AI Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Among the most deadly and complex illnesses in the world, pancreatic cancer is typified by its early asymptomatic stage and subsequent discovery of the disease when it has progressed to an advanced stage. Getting the patients in a correct treatment path at the earliest point is important for suitable intervention and patient outcomes in the long run. We utilized advanced algorithms and model prediction techniques includes, feature extraction, hyperparameter tuning and explainability methods which aims to enhance both the comprehension and predictive accuracy of models employed. The goal is to assess patient health status and diagnose pancreatic diseases (cancer vs. non-cancer) by developing a learning algorithm. We obtained a dataset containing demographic information and urine biomarkers to start the investigation. First stage of our analysis employs a single classifier and later we apply bagging and boosting algorithms to achieve ensemble models. Hyperparameter fine-tuning has got a positive outcome, which has Gradient Boosting and Cat Boosting as its top performing models. The ensemble model produced excellent results $(92.02 \%)$, demonstrating the usefulness of the suggested approach. LIME and SHAP techniques play the key role in model outcome interpretability providing an insight of algorithmic decision-making process. Such a wide range of combinations of biomarkers have a potential of pancreatic cancer detection in early stages and thus will help shape diagnostics strategies in near future.

articleTitle: An integrated color and texture feature based mango ripening stage classification from thermal imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Mango is a prominent fruit cultivated extensively in tropical and subtropical regions, serving as a significant economic asset for many countries. As Ensuring quality for export markets is essential, it traditionally achieved through labor-intensive and time-consuming manual sorting. Recently, computer vision (CV) based sorting has gained attention due to its efficiency and accuracy. While CV models leveraging RGB images can identify raw, ripened, and defective mangoes, certain internal defects and instances where raw and ripened mangoes exhibit similar coloration pose challenges, often leading to misclassification. In this study, we explore the use of thermal imaging to classify mangoes into raw, ripened, and defective categories. Our approach combines color and texture features from thermal images, excluding temperature data, while improving classification accuracy compared to previous studies. We conducted a comparative analysis of classification performance using various traditional classifiers, including Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). Our findings indicate that the combination of GLCM (contrast, correlation) and color features achieved a $87 \%$ accuracy rate with the SVM classifier for thermal images. It is also verified that the use of a simple Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model has increased the accuracy up to $97 \%$. However, this improvement in accuracy can only be robustly confirmed with a larger dataset.

articleTitle: Talk to Your Brain: Artificial Personalized Intelligence for Emotionally Adaptive AI Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The process of =making an Artificial intelligent system to replicating human emotional understanding and adapt its responses contextually by tailoring its responses based on individual cognitive and emotional states is called Artificial Personalized Intelligence (API). In this paper, we present a finetuned emotionally adaptive AI pipeline capable of generating personalized, human-like responses. Using a custom dataset based on six universal emotions—Sadness, Happiness, Fear, Anger, Surprise, and Disgust—collected from interviews with 30 participants, we have explored two approaches: fine-tuning a LLaMA-3 8B model with the Low-Rank Adapter (LoRA) technique and employing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agent-based framework over the same LLaMA-3 8B model. Emotion classification, prompt engineering, and model fine-tuning were used over the dataset to capture emotional and personalized subtleties in the responses based on different individuals. We conducted a comprehensive analysis, evaluating performance across candidates, emotions, and overall performance, using metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Pearson Correlation Coefficient to measure the difference among the outputs from both pipelines and actual human emotional responses. Our results show that prompt engineering combined with LoRA-based fine-tuning significantly enhances the ability to engage in emotionally intelligent and personalized conversations, whereas the RAG-based approach underperformed due to the pretrained LLAMA-3 model’s restrictive neutral and adversarial training. This highlights that fine-tuned LLMs are effective in replicating human emotions for personalized intelligence.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Sensitive Medical Data Sharing Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The aim of digital healthcare systems and the Internet of Medical Things (IOMT) is the ease of accessing high-quality healthcare from the comfort of one’s own residence.Therefore, the widespread implementation of home-based healthcare systems is the goal of IoMT. Millions of lives can be saved by developing intelligent and effective systems for the early detection of serious diseases, which also reduces the load on established healthcare institutions like hospitals.Patients and physicians now have access to real-time data because to IOT advancements. Because of this breakthrough’s use of effective sensors and communication technologies, digital healthcare systems are now less expensive and energy-intensive. This document introduces a method, for handling security and privacy issues related to the gathering, storage and use of data in a healthcare setting. Sensitive genetic data is securely transmitted and stored using a novel protocol through use of homomorphic encryption (FHE). Users can upload their data to cloud servers where it is encrypted and stored.Furthermore, the use of homomorphic encryption eliminates the need for encryption decryption cycles, guaranteeing data security, and enables AI models to be trained directly upon encrypted data. Additionally, The encrypted anonymous data may be shared for training purposes with outside organisations. Finally, the article examines various digital innovations in the healthcare context, their opportunities, limitations, and current challenges facing the e-health industry.

articleTitle: A Novel Multimodal Framework for Early Detection of Congestive Heart Failure using Ensemble Learning based Fusion Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In recent years, critical heart conditions like myocardial infarction (MI), congestive heart failure (CHF), pulmonary diseases, and non-communicable diseases have become increasingly prevalent. CHF, in particular, poses a significant threat with high mortality rates. It is defined by the heart’s incapacity to pump blood effectively, which causes the body to retain fluid. Various studies have focused on early diagnosis of heart failure using machine learning (ML) algorithms such as Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and Deep Learning (DL) models like Tiny Unet. However, these methods heavily rely on signal processing and manual analysis of ECG data, resulting in complexity and reduced accuracy. In order to tackle these challenges, we suggest a multimodal framework for CHF classification using ECG data. This framework extracts discriminatory features from pre-processed data and integrates the accuracy of ensemble learning models. Our approach achieves ${9 8. 5 2 \%}$ accuracy, indicating its potential for clinical use. Future research should explore additional features and modalities to enhance predictive modeling and extend ensemble learning for better MI detection, thereby improving cardiovascular health monitoring in clinical settings.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Pretrained Vision Transformer and VGG16 Models for Soil Moisture Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Accurate soil moisture monitoring is of prime importance to precision agriculture, water resource management, as well as for environmental monitoring. Traditional methods often suffer due to limited spatial coverage and manual data collection. Recent advancements in computer vision have significantly enhanced the ability to comprehend and analyse image data. These technological breakthroughs have made it possible for accurate and efficient image classification to find its way into computer vision as well as the realm of machine learning. This study introduces a comparative analysis of soil moisture classification using a pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT) and VGG16 models using high-resolution RGB images to classify dry and wet soil. The model was trained on a new dataset of 1028 images of soils taken from agricultural fields and outdoor locations. VGG16 had excellent train, validation, and test accuracies at 98.42%, 96.41%, and 95.96%, respectively, and was superior to the ViT model at 97.86%, 90.41%, and 91.13%. This is due to the ability of the VGG16 model to more effectively capture local spatial features and also its robustness against input variations and noise within the soil image dataset. Moreover, the efficient inference time of 70 ms attributed to the VGG16 architecture makes it generally well-suited for real-time applications in precision agriculture and environmental sensing.

articleTitle: Artery Vein Segmentation in Handheld Fundus Camera Retinal Images and leveraging Cross Entropy for improved Semantic performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The segmentation of retinal vessels into arteries and veins in retinal images is a crucial task for analysing the vascular changes with respect to many diseases that manifest ocular symptoms. But most existing research has concentrated on fundus images acquired using tabletop cameras and not much has been studied on images captured by handheld cameras. Such cameras are particularly useful for examining bedridden patients, especially those who may have conditions such as hypertension or diabetes that can affect the retina, since they are portable and can be easily maneuvered by healthcare providers, allowing them to perform retinal examinations conveniently at the patient’s bedside. This paper presents an approach to segment such images and assesses the impact of data augmentation on model performance. It further presents a method to compute pixel level weights during training, that allows for fine-grained adjustment of the loss function.

articleTitle: Advancing Medical Imaging: A Comparative Exploration of Generative Adversarial Networks for Chest X-ray Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Chest X-ray imaging is essential for diagnosing and treatment planning of individuals with diseases like COVID-19, Tuberculosis, and Pneumonia. However, creating efficient machine-learning algorithms for early detection is made difficult by a lack of labeled medical images. The study investigates the possibility of using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to create synthetic chest X-ray images for various lung diseases in order to address this issue. This study compares three distinct GAN architectures: Progressive Growing of Generative Adversarial Network (ProGAN), Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN), and Auxiliary Classifier Generative Adversarial Network (ACGAN). Acknowledging constraints within existing GAN architectures, the study employs a hybrid methodology. To improve training stability and image quality, this method combines the progressive generation of ProGAN with the Gradient Penalty loss of Wasserstein GAN (WGAN-GP). An InceptionV3 classifier was used to assess the quality of the generated images. On the original dataset, this classifier recorded an accuracy of 91%. The classifier achieved $72.08 \%, 68.62 \%$, and 45.50% accuracy on images generated by ProGAN, DCGAN, and ACGAN, respectively. The study demonstrates GANs potential to assist in alleviating data scarcity, hence improving the precision and effectiveness of machine learning algorithm training.

articleTitle: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 12 classification through Structural MRI: Insights from Regional Brain Volume and Cortical Thickness Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA) type 12 is a neurodegenerative hereditary disorder of progressive nature with a particularly high prevalence in India. This investigation evaluates the potential application of structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) data in the automated classification of SCA12. We acquired 32 SCA12 patients and 28 healthy controls for binary classification. Feature extraction was performed via three brain atlases - Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL3), Neuromorphometrics atlas, and Destrieux atlas. Subsequently, the ReliefF feature selection algorithm was employed to select the most informative features for analysis. Finally, two machine learning models, a linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) and radial basis kernel SVM (RBSVM), were implemented. Both models underwent training with a forward feature selection approach combined with leave-one-out cross-validation. The model achieved an optimal classification accuracy of $88.33 \%$ when features were constructed using gray matter volumes using the AAL3 atlas. It was observed that gray matter, white matter, and cortical thickness are better biomarkers than CSF volume for differentiating SCA12 patients. Additionally, biomarkers identified via feature selection may enhance the efficiency of clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Multilingual BERT-Based Framework for Robust Online Hate Speech Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Hate speech poses a significant threat to societal harmony and safety, often inciting violence and discrimination. Recent real-time incidents, such as the communal unrest in various parts of the world triggered by inflammatory online content, demonstrates the need for effective hate speech detection mechanisms. In this paper, we present a comprehensive hate speech detection model utilizing the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) algorithm, leveraging advanced Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. Our model is designed to address the challenges of detecting hate speech within the Hinglish language, a code-mixed variant combining Hindi and English. We used a pre-trained BERT model and tailored that model to function in real-time scenarios, offering robust and in-depth analysis capabilities. We adopted a multilingual and multimodal approach, enabling our system to detect hate speech. This task is accomplished across various content formats, including text, audio, video, images, GIFs, and YouTube video comments. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves an accuracy of 0.88. This underlines the model’s efficacy in detecting hate speech, showcasing its potential for application in diverse real-world contexts.

articleTitle: Ambiguous Boundary Uncertainty Reduction in Single Stage Detector Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The MS-COCO dataset provides ground truth bounding boxes with high accuracy, leaving minimal room for ambiguity. However, during the annotation process, uncertainties can still arise, particularly in situations where object boundaries are indistinct or when numerous annotators are involved. In this paper, we introduce a novel bounding box regression loss that improves the bounding box localization accuracy during the inference phase, particularly in scenarios characterized by the aforementioned uncertainties. During training, we also experiment with a thresholding procedure at the time of loss computation, which leverages the Intersection over Union (IoU) value, consequently enhancing the stabilization and precision of the bounding box localization. We evaluate the novel loss on multiple datasets focusing especially on metal surface defect datasets, yielding favorable results. When tested on the MSCOCO dataset for small object detection, we observe a gain in the Average Recall for small objects ($\mathbf{A R}^{\mathrm{S}}$) and Average Precision with 0.5 IoU value ($\mathrm{AP}^{0.5}$) of YOLOv7 by 1.83% and 1.61% respectively. We also validate the algorithm using other metal defects datasets, namely GC10-DET, and proprietary custom aircraft surface metal defects dataset, with consistently positive outcomes with up to 19.41% gain in Precision, 60.20% gain in Recall, 43.48% gain in mAP@. 5 and 46.86% gain in mAP@.5:.95 for some classes.

articleTitle: Unleashing Password Potential: VAEs vs GANs in a Password Guessing Duel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Insecure passwords remain a persistent vulnerability in cybersecurity. This study investigates the potential of employing Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) as tools for generating synthetic passwords, with the aim of enhancing existing password cracking methodologies. These models, trained on a dataset of leaked RockYou passwords, are evaluated based on their capacity to produce passwords that replicate the complexity and diversity observed in real-world passwords. Through a thorough assessment of the quality and characteristics of these synthetic passwords, this research reveals the strengths and weaknesses of each model. Additionally, the study examines the effectiveness of utilizing synthetic passwords in password cracking endeavors, comparing their performance to established methods and actual breached passwords. In conclusion, this research seeks to deepen our comprehension of password creation patterns and fortify our ability to counter the risks associated with weak passwords. By delving into the potential of VAEs and GANs, we contribute to the ongoing pursuit of robust cybersecurity measures and the safeguarding of sensitive information.

articleTitle: Video Based Steganography for Audio using LSB Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of information security, video steganography offers a promising solution for concealing sensitive data within multimedia content. The proposed approach introduces a novel approach that integrates video compression, audio embedding, and encryption to enhance security and efficiency in information transmission. The method follows a three-stage process, H.264 video compression to reduce file size, audio embedding using Least Significant Bit (LSB) steganography to conceal data within video frames, and Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) encryption to ensure robust cryptographic protection. Key findings demonstrate that H.264 compression effectively reduces video size while maintaining quality, LSB embedding conceals audio with minimal visual impact, and GCM encryption provides robust protection against unauthorized access and tampering. This comprehensive method offers a viable solution for secure, covert information transmission in multimedia, addressing critical needs in modern information security by combining steganography, compression, and encryption for a more robust and efficient approach than traditional methods.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Ensemble Learning Techniques for Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The paper employed a range of ensemble learning techniques to forecast Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) levels in Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTP). By harnessing ensemble learning, the main objective is to enhance the accuracy and robustness of COD prediction models by capitalizing on the diverse strengths of multiple algorithms. Our experiment encompassed two distinct WWTP datasets, allowing us to comprehensively assess the efficiency and effectiveness of three ensemble methods. Firstly, Bagging operates by creating multiple versions of a predictor and combining their outputs to form an aggregated prediction. Secondly, Boosting algorithms such as AdaBoost, GBM, and XGBoost sequentially constructed powerful learners, focusing on previously misclassified instances to bolster predictive performance. Finally, Stacking methodologies combined predictions from multiple models using a meta-learner. The analysis of the results for various models across the two wastewater treatment plant datasets (WWTPDS1 and WWTPDS2) reveals distinct performance levels. The Bagging model exhibits a reasonable performance with WWTPDS1 (MSE: 0.0016, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>: 0.9351) and a slightly lower performance with WWTPDS2 (MSE: 0.0033, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>: 0.6787). The Boosting model outperforms with lower MSE and higher $\mathrm{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ values for both datasets (WWTPDS1 MSE: 0.0010, $\mathbf{R}^{2}$: 0.9751; WWTPDS2 MSE: 0.0028, $\mathrm{R}^{2}: 0.7384$), indicating its better predictive accuracy and reliability. The Stacking model evaluated in the training phase, it showcases exceptionally low MSE and high $\mathrm{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ values (WWTPDS1 MSE: 0.0004, $\mathrm{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$: $\mathbf{0. 9 7 1 2;}$ WWTPDS2 MSE: $0.0009, R^{2}: 0.9213$). In the testing phase, the Stacking model maintains strong performance (WWTPDS1 MSE: 0.0013, $R^{2}: \mathbf{0. 9 4 9 4}$; WWTPDS2 MSE: 0.0028, $\mathrm{R}^{2}: \mathbf{0. 7 1 9 1)}$.

articleTitle: Stochastic Variations for Latent Data Representation (SVLDR): A Probabilistic Generative Modeling Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative enhancement method to Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) by integrating uncertainty into the latent representations, enabling the generation of more diverse and realistic data samples. Traditional VAEs often face limitations in exploring the latent space, leading to less variability in generated outputs. To address this, the proposed method incorporates controlled uncertainty in the latent space, facilitating a more comprehensive exploration of potential data configurations. Additionally, we propose a novel two-stage approach where a small neural network, trained on synthetic data drawn from a standard normal distribution, transforms the uncertain latent representation into a Gaussian prior. This transformation enhances the fidelity of the latent space, improving the quality of the generated samples. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated using the MNIST dataset, a benchmark for generative modeling, and evaluated using the Negative Log Likelihood (NLL) metric thereby assessing both the quality and diversity of generated samples. This method has broad applications, including data augmentation, anomaly detection, semi-supervised learning, and generating diverse samples for creative tasks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity Resilience with CYBRANA: A Cyber YARA/YAML-Based Resilience Firewall Solution Applied with Next-Gen AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The ever-increasing volume of server requests puts digital infrastructure at more risk of cyberattacks. This paper introduces CYBRANA, a cyberattack detection and mitigation system powered by AI. CYBRANA uses a Random Forest model to look into firewall and server logs for potential malicious threats. After analysis of flagged logs to extract request paths, CYBRANA then maps YAML rules to look for known attack pattern detection. Upon successful detection, CYBRANA classifies the attack type and severity (using CVSS scoring) by mapping it to the MITRE CAPEC framework®. This approach bridges the gap between existing cybersecurity frameworks and server log analysis, enabling a novel security pipeline. By automating threat detection and mitigation, CYBRANA enhances the security posture of digital infrastructure.

articleTitle: Enhancing Credit Card Fraud Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Anomaly Detection Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Financial fraud poses a major threat to financial service institutions and clients, necessitating advanced anomaly detection capabilities. This paper delves into related deep learning models which can be be used to differentiate and detect fraudulent transactions from normal transactions and flag anomalies. Challenges include evolving attack strategies, class imbalance, and model interpret-ability. The proposed methods utilize of a synergistic combination of ensemble learning techniques and unsupervised deep neural networks, like autoencoders and recurrent neural networks. The outcomes exhibit reliable results on credit card transaction datasets. A comprehensive comparative analysis follows to compare the proposed approach to traditional fraud detection methods, demonstrating its superiority in accurately identifying fraudulent transactions, adapting to emerging threats, handling high-dimensional data, and mitigating class imbalances with respect to data privacy and security.

articleTitle: An Efficient Image Contrast Enhancement using Segmentation in Genetic Algorithm for Remote Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optimized histogram equalization technique using a genetic algorithm (GA) for brightness-preserved contrast enhancement. This method optimizes the histogram equalization technique to extract detailed data from distorted images. The principal objective is to enhance histogram equalization by fixing a trade-off between contrast improvement and mean-brightness preservation. A genetic algorithm is used to generate the new target histogram. The optimized histogram is used in the histogram equalization (HE) process to generate the final enhanced image. The performance of the proposed method is checked and validated with qualitative and quantitative assessments against well-known state-of-the-art techniques. The result section depicts that the proposed method significantly enhances the visual effect of distorted images based on human subjective and objective evaluation indices. 3-5 percent enhancement can be observed if we compare the standard Histogram Equalization method to the proposed method.

articleTitle: A survey on the modern research on deep learning-based object detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Detecting objects remains a vital and challenging aspect within computer vision applications. Substantial progress in detecting objects is made by enhancing how objects are represented and by utilizing deep models of neural networks. This paper delivers a broad survey on the advancements on object detection within the deep learning era in recent years. Object detection algorithms are generally branded into two broad types centered on their training approach: single-stage detection algorithms and two-stage detection algorithms, each utilizing unique methods for pinpointing objects in images. We examine the underlying rationale of these algorithms by conducting experiments to compare various aspects, including quality metrics, trade-offs between speed/accuracy, and modelling practices. This study also provides a comparative assessment of leading convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used in detecting objects, emphasizing each model’s strengths/limits and presenting key conclusions. To foster a deeper understanding, we also identify areas for future research and potential advancements in object detection models within the domain of deep learning.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Fusion: CNN-GRU Model for Tuberculosis Detection Enhanced with LIME Interpretability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Substantial technological advances and extensive accessibility of medical data such as CT scans, X-rays and MRI images, have significantly driven the growth of automated detection systems for disease diagnosis. These Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems help healthcare providers make accurate diagnoses, particularly for infectious diseases that pose potentially fatal risks to patients. Extensive research endeavors have been undertaken, employing a combination of deep learning techniques alongside chest X-rays (CXRs) and CT scan images, to address a spectrum of pulmonary disorders, including tuberculosis (TB). This research study investigates the fusion of a traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), specifically the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), to improve the categorisation of CXRs into tuberculosis and normal categories. The GRU’s representation learning capability is leveraged as it learns from the attributes identified by the CNN and passed on to the model. This capability plays a crucial role in our study, as it enables the model to capture sequential patterns and dependencies within the extracted features. The hypothesis is that this ability will optimize the model’s detection efficiency in identifying TB from CXRs, thereby enhancing the classification accuracy. To address the challenge of an unbalanced dataset, various data augmentation methods have been applied, followed by image enhancement techniques. Additionally, the LIME package has been utilized to obtain interpretable explanations for individual predictions by highlighting key features used by the model in classification. The proposed model achieved an impressive accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and AUC of $\mathbf{9 8. 0 0 \%, 9 9. 4 3 \%, \mathbf { 9 6. 6 7 \% }, \mathbf { 9 8. 0 2 \% } \ 2 0}$ and 1.0 in correctly predicting target classes. The results establish that the proposed system performs well owing to the combination of CNN with GRU, which allows for the successful extraction of complex patterns from CXRs along with the capture of temporal dependencies within the data.

articleTitle: SERNet-Former: Segmentation by Efficient-ResNet with Attention-Boosting Gates and Attention-Fusion Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This research proposes an encoder-decoder architecture with a unique, efficient residual network, Efficient-ResNet. Attention-boosting gates and modules are fused with the feature-based semantic information and the output of the global context of the efficient residual network in the encoder. The decoder network is developed with additional attention-fusion networks inspired by the attention-boosting modules. Attention-fusion networks are designed to efficiently improve the one-to-one conversion of semantic information by deploying additional convolution layers in the decoder part. Our network is tested on the challenging CamVid and Cityscapes datasets. The proposed methods in this research improve the residual networks significantly. To the best of our knowledge, the developed network, SERNet-Former, achieves state-of-the-art results (84.62% mean IoU) on the CamVid dataset and challenging results (87.35% mean IoU on the validation dataset) on the Cityscapes datasets.

articleTitle: Fingerprint Liveliness Detection using Stacked Ensemble and Transfer Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The effectiveness and dependability of fingerprint recognition systems make them popular for biometric authentication. This research addresses the challenge of distinguishing between real and spoof fingerprint images using a comprehensive approach that integrates data preprocessing, data augmentation, feature extraction with pretrained models and stacked classifiers. The study begins with rigorous data preprocessing techniques to enhance the quality and consistency of the fingerprint images. Subsequently, data augmentation is employed to increase the diversity of the training dataset, enabling better generalization and robustness of the classification model. Feature extraction is then performed using pretrained convolutional neural network models, namely ResNet50, VGG16, and DenseNet201, to capture discriminative features from the fingerprint images.Stacked classifiers leverage the complementary strengths of multiple base classifiers, such as Random Forest, Extra Trees, and Support Vector Classifier, to improve classification performance. The proposed ensemble learning approach achieves an impressive accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9 . 3 0 \%}$ in distinguishing between real and spoof fingerprint images, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing biometric security systems.

articleTitle: Autoencoded Image Compression for Secure and Fast Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: With exponential growth in the use of digital image data, the need for efficient transmission methods has become imperative. Traditional image compression techniques often sacrifice image fidelity for reduced file sizes, challenging maintaining quality and efficiency. They also compromise security, leaving images vulnerable to threats such as man-in-the-middle attacks. This paper proposes an autoencoder architecture for image compression to not only help in dimensionality reduction but also inherently encrypt the images. The paper also introduces a composite loss function that combines reconstruction loss and residual loss for improved performance. The autoencoder architecture is designed to achieve optimal dimensionality reduction and regeneration accuracy while safeguarding the compressed data during transmission or storage. Images regenerated by the autoencoder are evaluated against three key metrics: reconstruction quality, compression ratio, and one-way delay during image transfer. The experiments reveal that the proposed architecture achieves an SSIM of 97.5% over the regenerated images and an average latency reduction of 87.5%, indicating its effectiveness as a secure and efficient solution for compressed image transfer.

articleTitle: AI in Ophthalmic Imaging: Enhancing Retina Analysis for Early Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In this review, we analyze the AI-based methods for retina segmentation and classification in ophthalmology/medical imaging with depth. This study comprises the whole research pipeline, including data retrieval and preprocessing, feature extraction classification as well as segmentation. It explores a mixture of machine and deep learning algorithms for these tasks, monitoring their performance using relevant metrics. Illustrating the stakes using early-onset disease detection in retinal image analysis, this review describes manual annotation limitation and provides outlines for AI solutions. It provides information on datasets used in previous works, describing their features and preprocessing procedures. This review details feature extraction from traditional image processing to deep learning, focusing on characteristic features for differentiating retinal abnormalities. The classification part describes several models used to classify the retinal images and its evaluation in terms of Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1-score. The proposed work also shows approaches to segment the region of interest in retina images and scoring mechanism such as Dice Coefficient, Intersection Over Union for evaluating segmentation. The article closes by reviewing summary points, stating limitations and directions for future research. To sum up, this all-in-one article is beneficial for academia and industry professionals not only to reveal the state-of-the-art techniques but also provide a guideline toward future research in AI-based solutions with improved diagnosis & treatment of retinal diseases.

articleTitle: TexAVi: Generating Stereoscopic VR Video Clips from Text Descriptions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: While generative models such as text-to-image, large language models and text-to-video have seen significant progress, the extension to text-to-virtual-reality remains largely unexplored, due to a deficit in training data and the complexity of achieving realistic depth and motion in virtual environments. This paper proposes an approach to coalesce existing generative systems to form a stereoscopic virtual reality video from text. Carried out in three main stages, we start with a base text-to-image model that captures context from an input text. We then employ Stable Diffusion on the rudimentary image produced, to generate frames with enhanced realism and overall quality. These frames are processed with depth estimation algorithms to create left-eye and right-eye views, which are stitched side-by-side to create an immersive viewing experience. Such systems would be highly beneficial in virtual reality production, since filming and scene building often require extensive hours of work and post-production effort. We utilize image evaluation techniques, specifically Fréchet Inception Distance and CLIP Score, to assess the visual quality of frames produced for the video. These quantitative measures establish the proficiency of the proposed method. Our work highlights the exciting possibilities of using natural language-driven graphics in fields like virtual reality simulations.

articleTitle: Advances in Crop Classification Using Satellite Imagery: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Classifying crop is essential for monitoring agricultural landscapes, managing re sources and assessing crop health. Crop classification is revolutionized by recent developments in satellite imagery and machine learning, with various datasets like multispectral, hyper-spectral, and SAR. Various machine learning and deep learning algorithms, such as CNNs, ANNs, and ensemble methods, play a pivotal role in the automation of crop classification. Ongoing research in this field aims to address the limitations like the availability of ground truth data, cloud cover, and seasonal variability. Future possibilities in this field include integration of multi-sensor data, enhancing temporal and spatial resolution, and enabling real-time monitoring for precision agriculture and sustainable land management. This review paper is a valuable resource for researchers in agriculture, remote sensing, and machine learning. This paper also offers insight into the cutting-edge techniques and the transformative potential of crop classification in agriculture and global food security.

articleTitle: Fusion of 3D Convolutional Neural Network and Multifractal Features for High- and Low-grade Glioma Classification using Diffusion Tensor Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The classification of gliomas is essential for the accurate diagnosis and effective treatment planning of brain tumors, particularly in distinguishing between low-grade gliomas (LGG) and high-grade gliomas (HGG). Conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) based classification, although common, often relies on radiological expertise and can miss microstructural changes in the white matter due to the presence of a tumor. This study proposes a novel approach by integrating the potential of 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with multifractal features derived from Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) to improve the classification accuracy of LGG and HGG patients. MRI scans from 86 patients (n= 39 LGG and n=47 HGG) were processed to generate Fractional Anisotropy (FA), Axial Diffusivity (AD), Radial Diffusivity (RD), and Mean Diffusivity (MD) 3D Nifti images of tumor and normal-appearing white matter regions. Multifractal features were extracted and fused with 3D CNN-derived features from the DTI maps of these regions. The 3D CNN model achieved notable improvements in classification accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and area under the receiving operating characteristics score after integrating multifractal features. 3D CNN-derived features from FA and MD images combined with its multifractal features demonstrated the highest classification accuracy (94 % for FA and 92% for MD of tumor region). Additionally, a novel approach using principal component analyses was developed to explain the separability of LGG and HGG classes before and after integrating multifractal features with 3D CNN-derived features. Our findings suggest that incorporating multifractal features of DTI in a 3D CNN framework offers a robust approach for glioma classification, providing a detailed characterization of tumor impact on brain white matter tissue.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multimodal Biometric Fusion with DWT, LSTM, and Attention Mechanism for Face and Iris Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper introduces a new multimodal biometric system integrating facial and iris recognition using discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks enhanced with an attention mechanism. DWT is effective in extracting global and local features, and these extracted traits are addressed as instances of serial data to enable LSTMs to pick temporal connections in and provide context-specific continuations with continual regularity; other than these factors, improvement of the features has a major impact because attention emphasizes exactly on where more contextual contribution would occur with these elements to allow further contextual insights during the output phase. Experimental results show commendable gains in performance as compared with conventional systems, and achieves identification of up to $\mathbf{9 9 . 9 4 \%}$. It can be utilized in security environment where accurate identification with biometrics and proper authentication is highly needed. Framework: Features acquired from the DWT are integrated inside an LSTM network. Thus, it provides guidelines for both the structured feeding schedule and the organizing of time data, thus better facilitating biometric recognition. Though some progress has been made in optimizing biometric identification for individuals with varied features, there is still much to be done.

articleTitle: Accurate extraction of handwritten text line in complex document images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: As for handwritten text recognition, accurately detecting and recognizing text lines in complex document images remains challenging due to the lack of datasets with complex document images and high-quality annotations. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach that employs fully convolutional network for iterative refinement of coarse labels, resulting in enhanced and refined ground truth labels. These labels correct manual annotation errors and upgrade the quality of annotation. Meanwhile, we present an improve model Handwritten Text Extraction Network (HTENet) designed for the extraction of handwritten text lines in complex scenarios, which demonstrates substantial improvements in detection accuracy when trained with our refined labels. Our approach outperforms existing methods like Progressive Scale Expansion Network (PSENet) and DBNet, offering a promising direction for future research in complex document image processing. Main contributions include a label refinement method that minimizes manual annotation effort, the development of a more accurate text line detection model, and the creation of two complex document image datasets.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements in Microscopy Image Enhancement using Deep Learning: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Microscopy image enhancement plays a pivotal role in understanding the details of biological cells and materials at microscopic scales. In recent years, there has been a significant rise in the advancement of microscopy image enhancement, specifically with the help of deep learning methods. This survey paper aims to provide a snapshot of this rapidly growing state-of-the-art method, focusing on its evolution, applications, challenges, and future directions. The core discussions take place around the key domains of microscopy image enhancement of super-resolution, reconstruction, and denoising, with each domain explored in terms of its current trends and their practical utility of deep learning.

articleTitle: Octopus: A Latent Diffusion Model for Enhanced Text-Driven Manipulation in Image Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: By combining user interactivity and precise control over image attributes, the applications of text-based image synthesis can be vastly expanded. Thanks to recent advancements in developing state-of-the-art text-to-image models, we can now generate images with high fidelity and diversity. While a plethora of research focuses on improving the fidelity and diversity of images generated using text prompts, less focus is given to controlling the attributes or characteristics of the generated images. On the other hand, there have been advancements in image editing through text prompts, but most of these models lack the understanding of spatial knowledge and precise control over the objects present in the image, which makes the edited images lose much of their characteristics. To address these challenges, this study proposes a three-step methodology to introduce our text-driven image editing conditional diffusion model called “Octopus,” which has precise control over image attributes. To bring in control over image attributes, this study uses a similar methodology proposed in a recent study, which uses rich text to control image attributes while exploring different formats, including bold, footnotes, font size, and font color. Then this model is used along with a fine-tuned Large Language Model (Gemma), to create a dataset of image editing examples to train Octopus, which, given an input image and edit instructions, generates the precise edited image during inference. This study demonstrates the potential of this approach with a variety of compelling results.

articleTitle: Longitudinal Volumetric Study for the Progression of Alzheimer’s Disease from Structural MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is an irreversible neurode-generative disorder affecting millions of individuals today. The prognosis of the disease solely depends on treating symptoms as they arise and proper caregiving, as there are no current medical preventative treatments apart from newly developing drugs, which can, at most, slow the progression. Thus, early detection of the disease at its most premature state is of paramount importance. We performed a longitudinal study of structural MRI for certain test subjects with AD and temporal data selected randomly from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database. We implement a robust pipeline to study the data, including modern pre-processing techniques such as spatial image registration, skull stripping, inhomogeneity correction, and tissue segmentation using an unsupervised learning approach (hidden Markov field model) using intensity histogram information. The temporal data across multiple visits is used to study the structural change in volumes of these tissue classes, namely, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), grey matter (GM), and white matter (WM) as the patients progressed further into the disease. We also analyze the changes in features extracted, with a modified Mann-Kendall statistic to detect changes in volume trends for each patient. A monotonic decrease (85.31%, 95.54%) was observed for GM volumes consistent with clinical findings, whereas the CSF counterpart increased monotonically with varying confidence scores (69.85%, 85.31%, 95.54%). Even though it is observed that WM volumes do not follow a majority trend, they exhibit an intolerable shifting from the baseline according to individual prognosis.

articleTitle: Beyond Textual Analysis: Framework for CSAT Score Prediction with Speech and Text Emotion Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In today’s competitive landscape, accurately assessing customer satisfaction is crucial for business success. This paper presents an innovative methodology for call centers, leveraging advanced speaker diarization, sentiment analysis, and speech emotion recognition (SER) to gain a nuanced understanding of customer needs and preferences. By integrating these techniques, our approach predicts customer satisfaction scores (CSAT), empowering businesses to refine products, optimize services, and make data-driven decisions. Experimental validation demonstrates the effectiveness of our methodology in uncovering actionable intelligence from call center interactions, enabling businesses to enhance customer experience and drive continuous improvement.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Enhanced Transfer Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a critical complication associated with diabetes, often leading to vision loss and blindness if not identified and managed promptly. This project focuses on the early detection and classification of various DR stages, a vital step toward better patient outcomes. We utilize transfer learning with EfficientNetB3, a model recognized for its efficient performance in image classification tasks. Through fine-tuning on a dataset of retinal images and using ImageNet pre-trained weights, the model achieves a higher accuracy in categorizing images into five classes: Healthy, Mild DR, Moderate DR, Proliferative DR, and Severe DR.To further enhance model robustness, various data augmentation techniques—including rotations, zooms, and horizontal flips—are applied to improve diversity within the training data. The dataset is carefully partitioned into training, validation, and testing subsets, allowing for precise monitoring of the model’s generalization capabilities and accuracy across different DR stages. Comprehensive performance evaluation is conducted using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and a confusion matrix to analyze the model’s ability to accurately classify each DR stage. This robust approach shows great potential for advancing effective DR classification, ensuring timely and precise treatment strategies for patients at risk.

articleTitle: Identification of Standard Sensible Bands for the Study of Oil Spill from Multi-sensor and Multi-spectral Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Oil spills are a primary concern for environmental health, including aquatic ecosystems. The oil spill phenomenon generally happens in remote and inaccessible areas. Tracking and monitoring such phenomena with traditional methods and field surveys would be risky, costly, and time-consuming. Remote sensing imageries would be an efficient solution to overcome these challenges. Multispectral imagery (MSI) is advanced in both spatial and temporal resolution. In this article, multisensor imagery is used to identify the standard band imageries that are more sensible to the oil spill phenomenon. The four sensors, viz., Sentinel-2, Landsat-8, Landsat-9, and MODIS, are used for the study. The spatial resolution varies between 500 meters to 10 meters, whereas temporal resolution is between 16 days to one day. Three methods, Spectral Reflectance Curve (SRC), Band Separability Analysis (BSA), and Density Slicing (DS) are used for the analysis of spectral bands. It has been observed that Blue, Green, and SWIR2 are standard bands in all four sensors for the study of the oil spill phenomenon.

articleTitle: Symptom Based Medical Department Determination Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Within the umbrella of current developments in Natural Language Processing (NLP), this work tackles the crucial problem of effectively classifying patients based on symptoms, thereby assigning patients an appropriate medical speciality and thus improving clinical decision support models. We fine-tuned and explored the efficacy of state-of-the-art BERT-based models, namely DistilBERT and BERT ${ }_{\text {BASE }}$, for classifying patient symptoms into one of the six categories: internal medicine, cardiology, neurology, gastroenterology, dermatology, and infectious diseases. Our experiments observed that BERT ${ }_{\text {BASE }}$ achieved 98% accuracy, while DistilBERT achieved a slightly higher accuracy of 99% on a tweaked dataset of more than 5,000 items.

articleTitle: A BLEU Perspective on Text Generation: Markov vs. LSTM Models in Storytelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Natural language generation is one of the most pivotal factors that bridges the gap between creativity and intelligence between humans and automated machines that can act like humans. It is the driving agent for many applications ranging from simple chatbots to complex models like OpenAI’s ChatGPT. This paper explores two methods for natural language generation for storytelling; one being a probabilistic approach using Markov models and a deep learning approach that uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The objective of this paper is to generate well-articulated, meaningful random stories using seed text and a n-gram specification. The language generation model is trained on the Sherlock Holmes stories dataset. We measure their ability to create engaging stories and compare the results using BLEU scores. The findings offer insights into the potential of blending statistical models with modern deep learning techniques but also highlights the limitations of both models due to their varying complexities. While the Markov models provide substantially diverse and meaningful stories, the LSTM generates excellent outputs but with certain drawbacks with limited inputs and large runtimes.
